patch.value: Parallel lane partitioning is derived from the work_plan.json dependency DAG; only tasks with no cross-lane dependencies are assigned to separate lanes, minimizing merge conflict risk (K12). (DEC1)

Each lane operates in a namespaced workspace partition (C22) with scoped tool permissions and file-path restrictions enforced by the Task Lane Orchestrator (C13), preventing cross-lane contamination. (DEC5)
Integration merge ordering is deterministic and independent of wall-clock lane completion timing; patchsets are applied in a canonical order derived from the work_plan DAG, not arrival order. (DEC4)

The Integration stage (C18→C19→C20→C21) is a dedicated sub-flow with its own validation, review, and repair cycle; merge conflicts exceeding deterministic resolution thresholds trigger structured conflict reports and escalation (HITL or reroute). (DEC4)

Medium HITL strictness: HITL is triggered for unresolved merge conflicts, critical security findings, secrets detection, protected-path modifications, ChangeRequests, gate waivers, and integration-level critical findings; lane-level validation relies more on automated gates. (DEC3)
Writer/reviewer/judge separation and multi-vendor diversity are enforced by the Global Orchestrator (C11) routing policy across all lanes and integration stages. (DEC5)
Context packs are compiled per-lane (scoped) and per-integration-stage (full integrated state) by the orchestrator using deterministic selection rules with bounded size. (DEC5)

Acceptance is two-tiered: each lane must pass its scoped gates (build/test/lint per lane file set) before fan-in; the integrated state must pass full-repo validators, integration review, and all freeze closure gates before the bundle is released. (DEC6)
